note: Threshold values below are a design proposal, not a measured verdict. No real four-engine (ollama/llama.cpp/mlx/strata) common-result trial exists yet. These ceilings are sized for a WHOLE-MACHINE peak reading from an external OS-level sampler (qmu/research#211's host_ram_peak / gpu_vram_peak: /proc/meminfo and nvidia-smi, not a single process's RSS), so they are deliberately wider than a per-process ceiling for the same use case would be (compare qmu/research#205's peakRss, which is scoped to one process and not reused here for that reason). Recalibrate against a real trial's common JSON before publishing any adoption claim.

useCases.label: Interactive coding assistant
useCases.rationale: A developer workstation also runs the editor, language server and browser alongside the engine; the ceiling covers the whole machine's memory, not an isolated engine process.

useCases.label: Batch document summarization
useCases.rationale: A dedicated batch host runs little else alongside the job, so the ceiling is sized to a large single-GPU workstation rather than a shared machine.

useCases.label: Edge / offline device
useCases.rationale: Constrained hardware shares its entire memory budget with the OS and other apps; the ceiling covers the whole machine, not an isolated process.
